gen-gf-baumans-gf-fustat: Baumans opens its c like a wrench jaw, every line drawn at one thickness. Fustat follows in a plain sans of bent-tubing lines and wide gaps, so a long passage moves along smoothly and feels current.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gantari: Baumans has a wrench-shaped c and a stubborn, uniform line. Gantari, a plain sans that looks bent from wire, keeps its wide apertures friendly, so a long passage feels approachable and modern without any strain.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gayathri: Stiff, tubular, and a bit odd. Baumans keeps its monoline skeleton for attention-grabbing display work, while Gayathri, a sans-serif with gentle letterpress-style thick-thin shifts and open curves, handles the quiet job of carrying text.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-google-sans: Baumans brings a crescent-wrench c and one unchanging stroke. Google Sans is a plain sans with pulled-back terminals and no thick-thin shift, and that shared uniformity is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-google-sans-flex: A c shaped like an opened crescent wrench sets Baumans apart. Google Sans Flex, a sans-serif with ribbon-cut stroke ends and clean open curves, gives the pair its strongest quality: a shared tidy, machined look.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gothic-a1: Baumans draws a tube-like line of constant width, and its wrench-shaped c is hard to forget. Gothic A1, a plain sans with a splayed c terminal, is better at quiet reading than the heading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gotu: Gotu reads cleanly, with sturdy hairlines and open-mouthed e crossbars. Baumans holds one unvarying line while this sans-serif eases between thick and thin, and a slightly larger body size would let that show.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gowun-dodum: That crescent-wrench c, drawn in a line that never changes, is pure Baumans. Gowun Dodum, a plain sans with a wide-mouthed a and smooth tubular strokes, makes a long passage feel tidy and unhurried.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gudea: A wrench-wide c and a single line thickness mark Baumans out. Gudea, a plain sans with thread-thin curves and glass-clear gaps at the terminals, reads best around a modest size, and a touch larger would help.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-hanken-grotesk: Baumans is stiff and commanding, with a crescent-wrench c. Its strength is attention-grabbing display; Hanken Grotesk, a sans with a wire-bent look and wide channels into each counter, is better at steady reading.
